records.source: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן עַזָּ֑תָה וַיַּרְא־שָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And went Samson to Gaza, and he saw there a woman, a prostitute, and he went in to her.
pieces: Samson went to Gaza. There he saw a prostitute, and he went in and slept with her.

L.1: And Samson went to Gaza, and he saw there a woman, a prostitute, and he went in to her.

R.1: One day Samson went to Gaza, a Philistine city. There he saw a prostitute, and he slept with her.

decisions.choice: Gaza: a Philistine city on the coast
decisions.reason: Gaza was the southernmost of the five Philistine cities (Joshua 13:3), near the sea, far from Samson's home in Zorah. He walks alone into the heart of enemy land.

decisions.choice: a woman who was a prostitute
decisions.reason: As at Joshua 2:1, the word (zonah) is the ordinary word for a woman who sells sex. The story does not soften it.

decisions.choice: he went in to her: he had sex with her
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is a plain way of saying a man had sex with her (Genesis 16:4; 38:18). The chapter opens as Samson's story has run so far: he goes after what he sees (14:1-3).

decisions.choice: slept with her; Readable "a Philistine city"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "went in to her" means (m3). Readable also says what Gaza was (m1).

records.heading: Samson at Gaza

records.source: לַֽעַזָּתִ֣ים׀לֵאמֹ֗ר בָּ֤א שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ הֵ֔נָּה וַיָּסֹ֛בּוּ וַיֶּאֶרְבוּ־ל֥וֹ כָל־הַלַּ֖יְלָה בְּשַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיִּתְחָרְשׁ֤וּ כָל־הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עַד־א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר וַהֲרְגְנֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: To the Gazites, saying, has come Samson here. And they surrounded and lay in wait for him all the night at [the] gate of the city, and they kept quiet all the night, saying, until [the] light of the morning, and we will kill him.
pieces: The people of Gaza were told, "Samson has come here!" So they surrounded the place and lay in ambush for him at the city gate through the night. They made no move the whole night, for they said, "When morning light comes, we will kill him."

L.2: [It was told] to the Gazites, "Samson has come here." And they surrounded [the place] and lay in wait for him all night at the gate of the city. And they kept quiet all night, saying, "Until the light of the morning; then we will kill him."

R.2: Someone told the people of Gaza, "Samson is here!" So they surrounded the place. All night long they hid and waited for him at the city gate. They kept still the whole night. They said, "When it gets light in the morning, we will kill him."

decisions.choice: [It was told] to the Gazites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence has no verb: it says only "To the Gazites, saying". The ancient Greek translation reads "and it was told to the Gazites", which may keep a word lost from the Hebrew, or may simply supply what the sense needs. Either way the meaning is the same: someone brought word that Samson was in the city. This description comes from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked against its manuscripts.

decisions.choice: they kept quiet all night: they waited for dawn
decisions.reason: The men did nothing during the night. The city gate was shut at night, so they expected to catch Samson when it opened in the morning and he tried to leave.

decisions.choice: the gate of the city
decisions.reason: A walled city had one main gate, closed and barred at night (Joshua 2:5, 7). Anyone leaving had to pass through it, so it was the place for an ambush.

decisions.choice: [It was told] (L); were told / Someone told (B, R); [the place] (L)
decisions.reason: The verb the sense needs is supplied (m1), and so is the object of "surrounded", which the Hebrew leaves out.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב שִׁמְשׁוֹן֮ עַד־חֲצִ֣י הַלַּיְלָה֒ וַיָּ֣קָם׀בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֗יְלָה וַיֶּאֱחֹ֞ז בְּדַלְת֤וֹת שַֽׁעַר־הָעִיר֙ וּבִשְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּז֔וֹת וַיִּסָּעֵם֙ עִֽם־הַבְּרִ֔יחַ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־כְּתֵפָ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲלֵם֙ אֶל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And lay Samson until [the] middle of the night, and he arose in [the] middle of the night and took hold of [the] doors of [the] gate of the city and of [the] two posts and pulled them up with the bar, and put [them] on his shoulders and carried them up to [the] top of the hill that [is] before Hebron.
pieces: But Samson lay there only until midnight. At midnight he got up and seized the doors of the city gate together with its two posts, and he tore them loose, bar and all. Lifting them onto his shoulders, he carried them all the way up to the hilltop that faces Hebron.

L.3: And Samson lay until the middle of the night, and he arose at the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city and of the two doorposts, and pulled them up with the bar, and put [them] on his shoulders and carried them up to the top of the hill that [is] in front of Hebron.

R.3: But Samson stayed in bed only until midnight. Then he got up and went to the city gate. He grabbed its two doors and the two posts beside them. He pulled the whole gate out of the ground, with the bar that locked it. He put it all on his shoulders. Then he carried it up to the top of the hill that looks toward Hebron.

decisions.choice: the doors, the doorposts and the bar: the whole gate
decisions.reason: The bar was the beam laid across the closed doors to lock them. Samson tears out doors, posts and bar together. A city without its gate lay open to any enemy, and its people were put to shame.

decisions.choice: the hill in front of Hebron
alternatives: a hill near Gaza from which one looks toward Hebron
decisions.reason: Hebron lies in the hill country of Judah, about 40 miles from Gaza and some 3,000 feet higher. "In front of Hebron" may mean a hill near Hebron, or a hill on the way that faces toward it. Either way the gate of the Philistine city ends up on a hill in Israel's land.

decisions.choice: Samson lay until midnight
decisions.reason: The verb picks up verse 1: he stayed with the woman. Leaving at midnight, he escaped the men who were waiting for morning (verse 2).

decisions.choice: pulled the whole gate out of the ground, with the bar that locked it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bar was for and that the posts came out of the ground with the doors (m1).

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב אִשָּׁ֖ה בְּנַ֣חַל שֹׂרֵ֑ק וּשְׁמָ֖הּ דְּלִילָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was after thus, and he loved a woman in [the] valley of Sorek, and her name [was] Delilah.
pieces: Some time after this, he fell in love with a woman named Delilah, in the Valley of Sorek.

L.4: And it came about after this that he loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek, and her name [was] Delilah.

R.4: Later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah. She lived in the Valley of Sorek.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Sorek
decisions.reason: The valley runs west from the hills near Zorah and Eshtaol, Samson's home, down toward Philistine land; Timnah lay near it (14:1). It was border country between Israel and the Philistines. The name probably comes from a word for choice red grapes (Isaiah 5:2).

decisions.choice: Delilah: her people are not named
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Delilah was a Philistine or an Israelite, or that Samson married her. The Philistine rulers come to her as someone they can buy (verse 5). The meaning of her name is not certain.

decisions.choice: he loved a woman
decisions.reason: This is the first time the text says Samson loved a woman. It never says that Delilah loved him.

decisions.choice: fell in love with
decisions.reason: The verb describes the start of his love here, so Balanced and Readable say "fell in love"; Literal keeps "loved".

records.heading: Delilah and the secret of Samson's strength

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יהָ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֨אמְרוּ לָ֜הּ פַּתִּ֣י אוֹת֗וֹ וּרְאִי֙ בַּמֶּה֙ כֹּח֣וֹ גָד֔וֹל וּבַמֶּה֙ נ֣וּכַל ל֔וֹ וַאֲסַרְנֻ֖הוּ לְעַנֹּת֑וֹ וַאֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔ךְ אִ֕ישׁ אֶ֥לֶף וּמֵאָ֖ה כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And came up to her [the] rulers of [the] Philistines and said to her, entice him and see in what his strength [is] great and by what we will prevail over him, and we will bind him to humble him; and we, we will give you each a thousand and a hundred silver.
pieces: The rulers of the Philistines came up to her and said, "Coax him, and find out what makes his strength so great and how we can overpower him, so that we can tie him up and subdue him. Each of us will give you {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}}."

L.5: And the rulers of the Philistines came up to her and said to her, "Entice him, and see in what his great strength [lies], and by what we may overpower him, so that we may bind him to subdue him. And we will each give you 1,100 [shekels of] silver."

R.5: The rulers of the Philistines came to see her. They said, "Trick Samson into telling you his secret. Find out what makes him so strong. Find out how we can overpower him, so we can tie him up and make him helpless. If you do, each of us will pay you {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}}."

decisions.choice: the rulers of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The word (seren) is used only of the rulers of the five Philistine cities (Joshua 13:3; Judges 3:3) and may be a Philistine word. All five come together to deal with Samson.

decisions.choice: entice him: coax him into telling
decisions.reason: The verb means to persuade someone by charm or trickery. The Philistines said the same to Samson's wife at Timnah (14:15).

decisions.choice: to subdue him
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring someone low: to overpower him, and also to humiliate or mistreat him. It returns in verses 6 and 19.

decisions.choice: 1,100 pieces of silver from each ruler
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "1,100 silver"; the unit is the shekel, a weight. From five rulers that makes 5,500 shekels, a huge sum: a priest's yearly pay was ten shekels (17:10).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 28 pounds of silver|1,100 shekels of silver}}
decisions.reason: About 2/5 ounce to the shekel gives about 440 ounces, about 28 pounds. The units setting gives the original "1,100 shekels". Literal keeps the Hebrew count and brackets the unit it leaves out.

decisions.choice: Trick Samson into telling you his secret ... If you do
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "entice him" aims at (m2) and makes the condition of the payment plain.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל־שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֣ גָד֑וֹל וּבַמֶּ֥ה תֵאָסֵ֖ר לְעַנּוֹתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Delilah to Samson, tell, please, to me in what your strength [is] great and with what you may be bound to humble you.
pieces: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me what makes your strength so great, and what it would take to tie you up and subdue you."

L.6: And Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me in what your great strength [lies], and with what you could be bound so as to subdue you."

R.6: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me the secret of your great strength. How could someone tie you up and make you helpless?"

decisions.choice: Delilah asks openly
decisions.reason: Her question repeats the rulers' words almost exactly (verse 5), even "to subdue you". She hides nothing of what she wants, yet Samson goes on playing with her.

decisions.choice: the secret of your great strength
decisions.reason: Readable says "secret", since she is asking where his strength comes from.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִם־יַאַסְרֻ֗נִי בְּשִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־חֹרָ֑בוּוְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said to her Samson, if they bind me with seven bowstrings fresh that not have been dried, and I will be weak and I will be like one of the man.
pieces: Samson answered, "Suppose they tie me with seven fresh bowstrings that were never dried. Then I will become weak and be like any other man."

L.7: And Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, then I will become weak and be like any [other] man."

R.7: Samson told her, "If someone ties me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not dried out yet, I will lose my strength. I will be as weak as anyone else."

decisions.choice: fresh bowstrings: cords of gut or sinew
decisions.reason: The word (yeter) is a cord: a bowstring (Psalm 11:2) or a tent cord (Job 4:21). "Fresh, not dried" points to cords made from animal gut or sinew, still moist and supple.

decisions.choice: seven: a full number
decisions.reason: Seven stands for completeness. His hair too is in seven braids (verses 13, 19), so the number of his lie points toward the truth.

decisions.choice: like any other man: an ordinary human being
decisions.reason: "Like one of mankind" means no stronger than anyone else.

decisions.choice: bowstrings
decisions.reason: "Bowstrings" names the commonest use of the word and shows what kind of cord it was (m1).

records.source: וַיַּעֲלוּ־לָ֞הּ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים שִׁבְעָ֛ה יְתָרִ֥ים לַחִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־חֹרָ֑בוּ וַתַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And brought up to her [the] rulers of [the] Philistines seven bowstrings fresh that not had been dried, and she bound him with them.
pieces: So the Philistine rulers brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings, never dried, and she tied him up with them.

L.8: And the rulers of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

R.8: So the Philistine rulers brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not dried out. And she tied Samson up with them.

decisions.choice: she bound him
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Samson was awake or asleep, or how he let himself be tied. It moves straight to the test (verse 9).

records.source: וְהָאֹרֵ֗ב יֹשֵׁ֥ב לָהּ֙ בַּחֶ֔דֶר וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיְנַתֵּק֙ אֶת־הַיְתָרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִנָּתֵ֤ק פְּתִֽיל־הַנְּעֹ֨רֶת֙ בַּהֲרִיח֣וֹ אֵ֔שׁ וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע כֹּחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the ambush [was] sitting for her in the room. And she said to him, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And he snapped the bowstrings as snaps a strand of the tow when it smells fire. And not was known his strength.
pieces: She had men hidden in the inner room, waiting. Then she said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" But he snapped the bowstrings as easily as a strand of flax fiber snaps at the touch of fire. So the secret of his strength was still not found out.

L.9: Now the ambush was waiting for her in the inner room. And she said to him, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And he snapped the bowstrings as a strand of tow snaps when it smells fire. And his strength was not known.

R.9: Some men were hiding in the inner room, waiting. Delilah shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" But Samson broke the bowstrings as easily as a thread breaks when a flame touches it. So no one found out the secret of his strength.

decisions.choice: the ambush was waiting in the inner room
decisions.reason: "The ambush" means the men set to lie in wait. The room (cheder) is an inner room or bedroom (15:1), out of sight.

decisions.choice: as a strand of tow snaps when it smells fire
decisions.reason: Tow is the short, rough fibers left from flax. It catches fire at once. "When it smells fire" means when fire comes near it.

decisions.choice: his strength was not known: its source stayed hidden
decisions.reason: Everyone knew he was strong; what stayed unknown was where the strength came from and how to take it away.

decisions.choice: men hidden; the secret of his strength
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "the ambush" was (m1) and what was not known (m3).

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר דְּלִילָה֙ אֶל־שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הִנֵּה֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י כְּזָבִ֑ים עַתָּה֙ הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א לִ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Delilah to Samson, look, you have mocked me and spoken to me lies; now tell, please, to me with what you may be bound.
pieces: Then Delilah said to Samson, "You have made a fool of me and told me lies! Now please tell me what it would take to tie you up."

L.10: And Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have mocked me and told me lies. Now, please tell me with what you could be bound."

R.10: Delilah said to Samson, "You tricked me! You lied to me! Now please tell me. How can someone tie you up?"

decisions.choice: you have mocked me: you have made a fool of me
decisions.reason: The verb means to trifle with or deceive someone; Laban "cheated" Jacob with it (Genesis 31:7). Delilah complains of being lied to while she herself is lying to him.

decisions.choice: "Look" (L) is left out at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws attention to what follows. Balanced and Readable show that by the tone of her complaint instead.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם־אָס֤וֹר יַאַסְר֨וּנִי֙ בַּעֲבֹתִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־נַעֲשָׂ֥ה בָהֶ֖ם מְלָאכָ֑ה וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּאַחַ֥ד הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said to her, if binding they bind me with ropes new that not has been done with them work, and I will be weak and I will be like one of the man.
pieces: He said to her, "If they tie me up tightly with new ropes that have never been used for work, I will become weak and be like any other man."

L.11: And he said to her, "If they really bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I will become weak and be like any [other] man."

R.11: He said to her, "If someone ties me up tightly with brand-new ropes, ones never used for work, I will lose my strength. I will be like anyone else."

decisions.choice: if they really bind me: tie me up firmly
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled ("binding they bind"), a common Hebrew way of stressing an action: tied up properly and tight.

decisions.choice: new ropes: they had failed before
decisions.reason: The men of Judah had bound Samson with two new ropes, and he broke them like burnt flax (15:13-14). Delilah may not know it; the reader does.

decisions.choice: really (L); tightly (B, R)
decisions.reason: The doubled verb (m1) is shown by an adverb.

records.source: וַתִּקַּ֣ח דְּלִילָה֩ עֲבֹתִ֨ים חֲדָשִׁ֜ים וַתַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בָהֶ֗ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֤ים עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וְהָאֹרֵ֖ב יֹשֵׁ֣ב בֶּחָ֑דֶר וַֽיְנַתְּקֵ֛ם מֵעַ֥ל זְרֹעֹתָ֖יו כַּחֽוּט׃
records.gloss: And took Delilah ropes new and bound him with them, and she said to him, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And the ambush [was] sitting in the room. And he snapped them from upon his arms like thread.
pieces: So Delilah took new ropes and tied him up with them. Then she said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" Men were hidden in the inner room, waiting. But he snapped the ropes off his arms like thread.

L.12: So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and said to him, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And the ambush was waiting in the inner room. And he snapped them off his arms like a thread.

R.12: So Delilah got some new ropes and tied him up with them. Men were hiding in the inner room again. Delilah shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" But he broke the ropes off his arms as if they were thread.

decisions.choice: the ambush was waiting: already there
decisions.reason: The clause about the men in hiding comes after her cry, but it describes how things stood: they had been waiting all along, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: like thread
decisions.reason: A single spun thread, the weakest of cords. The test ends as the first did (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Men were hiding ... again, before her shout
decisions.reason: Readable puts the background first (m1), so the order of events is clear.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר דְּלִילָ֜ה אֶל־שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן עַד־הֵ֜נָּה הֵתַ֤לְתָּ בִּי֙ וַתְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַי֙ כְּזָבִ֔ים הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה תֵּאָסֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אִם־תַּאַרְגִ֗י אֶת־שֶׁ֛בַע מַחְלְפ֥וֹת רֹאשִׁ֖י עִם־הַמַּסָּֽכֶת׃
records.gloss: And said Delilah to Samson, until now you have mocked me and spoken to me lies; tell to me with what you may be bound. And he said to her, if you weave [the] seven braids of my head with the web.
pieces: Then Delilah said to Samson, "All this time you have been making a fool of me and telling me lies. Tell me what it would take to tie you up." He answered, "Weave the seven braids of my head into the fabric on the loom."

L.13: And Delilah said to Samson, "Until now you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with what you could be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven braids of my head with the web."

R.13: Delilah said to Samson, "You keep tricking me and telling me lies! Tell me how someone can tie you up." Samson said, "My hair is in seven braids. Weave them into the cloth on your loom."

decisions.choice: the shorter Hebrew text
alternatives: the longer text of the ancient Greek translation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence stops after "if you weave the seven braids of my head with the web" and never says what would happen; verse 14 goes straight to "she fastened [it] with the pin". The ancient Greek translation has a longer text here, roughly: "... with the web, and fasten [it] with the pin into the wall, then I will become weak and be like any other man. And while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his head and wove them into the web." It then reads in verse 14 "and she fastened [it] with the pin into the wall". The longer text follows the pattern of verses 7-8 and 11-12, where each lie is followed by its test, and a copyist's eye could easily have jumped from one "web" to the next and dropped a line. The meaning of the story does not change, only how fully it is told. This draft follows the Hebrew and notes the longer reading. The wording of the Greek is given from general knowledge and must be checked against its manuscripts before review.

decisions.choice: weave ... with the web: on a loom
decisions.reason: The web (massekhet) is the cloth on the loom, the warp threads with the weaving in progress. Samson's long hair would be worked into it like thread, pinning his head to the loom.

decisions.choice: the seven braids of my head
decisions.reason: His hair had never been cut (13:5) and was kept in seven locks or braids. With this answer he comes close to the truth: for the first time his hair is the subject (verse 17).

decisions.choice: until now: all this time
decisions.reason: Delilah complains that he has lied every time so far.

decisions.choice: Weave the seven braids ...: an instruction
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "if" with no "then" clause (m1). Balanced and Readable put his words as an instruction, which gives the same sense without leaving the sentence hanging; Literal keeps the bare "if".

records.source: וַתִּתְקַע֙ בַּיָּתֵ֔ד וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּיקַץ֙ מִשְּׁנָת֔וֹ וַיִּסַּ֛ע אֶת־הַיְתַ֥ד הָאֶ֖רֶג וְאֶת־הַמַּסָּֽכֶת׃
records.gloss: And she fastened with the pin, and she said to him, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom and the web.
pieces: So she wove his hair in and fastened it tight with the pin, and said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He woke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom along with the web.

L.14: And she fastened [it] with the pin, and said to him, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom, and the web.

R.14: So Delilah wove his hair into the cloth and fastened it tight with the pin. Then she shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" Samson woke up. He pulled out the pin of the loom, and the cloth with it.

decisions.choice: she fastened [it] with the pin
decisions.reason: As at verse 13: the Hebrew does not say what she fastened, and the ancient Greek translation has a longer text that tells how she wove his hair into the web while he slept and pinned it "into the wall". The Hebrew implies the same: he was asleep, and the web came away with his hair.

decisions.choice: the pin
decisions.reason: The word (yated) is a peg or pin; it is the tent peg Jael drove through Sisera's head (4:21-22). Here it is the weaving pin that held the work tight on the loom.

decisions.choice: the pin of the loom, and the web
alternatives: the pin, the loom and the web
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists "the pin, the loom, and the web". It is read as the loom's pin together with the woven cloth: he pulled his head free and tore it all away.

decisions.choice: she wove his hair in / wove his hair into the cloth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what verse 13 and his pulling out the web imply: she did weave his hair in before pinning it (m1). This is not taken from the longer Greek text; the Hebrew story needs it.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֚יךְ תֹּאמַ֣ר אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ וְלִבְּךָ֖ אֵ֣ין אִתִּ֑י זֶ֣ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וְלֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י בַּמֶּ֖ה כֹּחֲךָ֥ גָדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And she said to him, how will you say, I love you, and your heart not [is] with me? These three times you have mocked me and not told me in what your strength [is] great.
pieces: Then she said to him, "How can you tell me, 'I love you,' while you keep your heart from me? Three times now you have made a fool of me, and you still have not told me what makes your strength so great."

L.15: And she said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' and your heart is not with me? These three times you have mocked me, and you have not told me in what your great strength [lies]."

R.15: Then she said to him, "How can you say that you love me? You do not trust me with what is in your heart. Three times now you have made a fool of me. You still have not told me why you are so strong."

decisions.choice: your heart is not with me: you do not open your mind to me
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self, the thoughts and will. A heart "not with" someone holds back from them. When he finally gives in, he tells her "all his heart" (verses 17-18).

decisions.choice: How can you say, 'I love you'?
decisions.reason: His wife at Timnah used the same weapon: "You only hate me; you do not love me" (14:16), and she too wore him down with tears for days.

decisions.choice: keep your heart from me (B); do not trust me with what is in your heart (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַ֠יְהִי כִּֽי־הֵצִ֨יקָה לּ֧וֹ בִדְבָרֶ֛יהָ כָּל־הַיָּמִ֖ים וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵ֑הוּ וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נַפְשׁ֖וֹ לָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And it was when she pressed him with her words all the days and urged him, and was short his soul to die.
pieces: Day after day she kept pressing him with her words and pleading with him, until he was weary to death of it.

L.16: And it came about, when she pressed him with her words every day and urged him, that his soul was short to the point of death.

R.16: Day after day she kept asking him and begging him. At last Samson was so tired of it that he felt he would die.

decisions.choice: his soul was short to the point of death
decisions.reason: To be "short of soul" is to lose patience, to be unable to bear something any longer (Numbers 21:4; Judges 10:16). "To death" makes it extreme: he was worn out completely.

decisions.choice: urged him
decisions.reason: A rare verb meaning to press or push someone hard. With "pressed him" it shows how steady her pressure was.

decisions.choice: weary to death of it (B); so tired of it that he felt he would die (R)
alternatives: his soul was vexed to death
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "short of soul" means (m1).

records.source: וַיַּגֶּד־לָ֣הּ אֶת־כָּל־לִבּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהּ֙ מוֹרָה֙ לֹֽא־עָלָ֣ה עַל־רֹאשִׁ֔י כִּֽי־נְזִ֧יר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲנִ֖י מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֑י אִם־גֻּלַּ֨חְתִּי֙ וְסָ֣ר מִמֶּ֣נִּי כֹחִ֔י וְחָלִ֥יתִי וְהָיִ֖יתִי כְּכָל־הָאָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he told her all his heart and said to her, a razor not has come up on my head, for a Nazirite of God I [am] from [the] womb of my mother; if I am shaved, and will depart from me my strength, and I will be weak and I will be like all the man.
pieces: So he told her everything that was in his heart. "No razor has ever touched my head," he said to her, "because from my mother's womb I have been set apart to God as a Nazirite. If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become weak and be like any other man."

L.17: And he told her all his heart and said to her, "A razor has not come up on my head, for I [am] a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I am shaved, then my strength will leave me, and I will become weak and be like any [other] man."

R.17: So Samson told her his whole secret. He said, "My hair has never been cut. I have been a Nazirite since before I was born. That means I was set apart to serve God. If someone shaved my head, my strength would leave me. I would be as weak as anyone else."

decisions.choice: a Nazirite of God
decisions.reason: A Nazirite was a person set apart to God by a vow: no razor on the head, no wine or grape products, no touching a dead body (Numbers 6:1-21). Most took the vow for a time; Samson was given to it for life before his birth (13:5, 7).

decisions.choice: if I am shaved, my strength will leave me
decisions.reason: The strength was not in the hair as such. The uncut hair was the sign that he belonged to God, and the strength came from the Spirit of the LORD (14:6, 19; 15:14). When the sign is gone, the narrator says, the LORD had left him (verse 20).

decisions.choice: he told her all his heart: the whole truth
decisions.reason: He held nothing back. The same words return in verse 18, where Delilah sees that this time he has told her everything.

decisions.choice: That means I was set apart to serve God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Nazirite (m1). "Since before I was born" gives the sense of "from my mother's womb".

records.source: וַתֵּ֣רֶא דְלִילָ֗הכִּֽי־הִגִּ֣יד לָהּ֮ אֶת־כָּל־לִבּוֹ֒ וַתִּשְׁלַ֡ח וַתִּקְרָא֩ לְסַרְנֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים לֵאמֹר֙ עֲל֣וּ הַפַּ֔עַם כִּֽי־הִגִּ֥יד לִ֖י אֶת־כָּל־לִבּ֑וֹ וְעָל֤וּ אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיַּעֲל֥וּ הַכֶּ֖סֶף בְּיָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And saw Delilah that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and called to [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, saying, come up this time, for he has told me all his heart. And came up to her [the] rulers of [the] Philistines and brought up the silver in their hand.
pieces: When Delilah saw that he had told her everything in his heart, she sent word to the rulers of the Philistines: "Come up just once more, for he has told me everything." So the rulers of the Philistines came up to her, bringing the silver with them.

L.18: And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and called the rulers of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart." And the rulers of the Philistines came up to her and brought up the silver in their hand.

R.18: Delilah could tell that this time Samson had told her the truth. So she sent a message to the Philistine rulers. She said, "Come back one more time. He has told me everything." So the rulers came, and they brought the silver with them to pay her.

decisions.choice: he has told me (in Delilah's message)
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text say "he has told her", but the reading marked in the margin for reading aloud is "he has told me". Since these are Delilah's own words, "me" fits; the written form may have been copied from the first half of the verse.

decisions.choice: Delilah saw: she could tell he spoke the truth
decisions.reason: The text does not say how she knew. This answer was different: it spoke of God and of his birth, not only of cords and ropes.

decisions.choice: they brought the silver in their hand
decisions.reason: The rulers come ready to pay what they had promised (verse 5).

decisions.choice: to pay her
decisions.reason: Readable says what the silver was for (m3).

records.source: וַתְּיַשְּׁנֵ֨הוּ֙ עַל־בִּרְכֶּ֔יהָ וַתִּקְרָ֣א לָאִ֔ישׁ וַתְּגַלַּ֕ח אֶת־שֶׁ֖בַע מַחְלְפ֣וֹת רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַתָּ֨חֶל֙ לְעַנּוֹת֔וֹ וַיָּ֥סַר כֹּח֖וֹ מֵעָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And she made him sleep on her knees and called for the man and she shaved [the] seven braids of his head, and she began to humble him, and departed his strength from upon him.
pieces: She lulled him to sleep on her lap and called for a man, and she had the seven braids of his head shaved off. Then she began to subdue him, and his strength had left him.

L.19: And she made him sleep on her knees, and called for a man, and she shaved off the seven braids of his head. And she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.

R.19: Delilah got Samson to fall asleep with his head on her lap. Then she called for a man to come and shave off the seven braids of his hair. Then Delilah began to mistreat him, and he was helpless. His strength was gone.

decisions.choice: on her knees: in her lap
decisions.reason: He fell asleep with his head on her lap, trusting her.

decisions.choice: she shaved: through the man she called
decisions.reason: The verb "shaved" is hers, but she had called a man for the task; the act was done at her command.

decisions.choice: she began to subdue him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verses 5-6: to bring low, overpower, mistreat. The ancient Greek translation reads "he began to be brought low", making Samson the subject; the Hebrew makes Delilah the one who begins to break him.

decisions.choice: had ... shaved off (B); called for a man to come and shave (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who used the razor (m2).

records.source: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר פְּלִשְׁתִּ֥ים עָלֶ֖יךָ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּקַ֣ץ מִשְּׁנָת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵצֵ֞א כְּפַ֤עַם בְּפַ֨עַם֙ וְאִנָּעֵ֔ר וְהוּא֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה סָ֥ר מֵעָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And she said, [the] Philistines [are] upon you, Samson! And he awoke from his sleep and said, I will go out as time in time and I will shake free. And he not knew that YHWH had departed from upon him.
pieces: Then she said, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He woke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as I did the other times and shake myself loose." But he did not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left him.

L.20: And she said, "The Philistines [are] upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as time after time, and shake myself free." But he did not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had departed from him.

R.20: Then she shouted, "Samson! The Philistines are here to get you!" Samson woke up. He said to himself, "I will get away, just like before. I will shake myself loose." But he did not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left him.

decisions.choice: the LORD had departed from him
decisions.reason: This is the real loss. Samson's strength came when the Spirit of the LORD rushed on him (14:6, 19; 15:14); with the sign of his vow gone, the LORD left him. The same words are later used of Saul (1 Samuel 16:14; 18:12).

decisions.choice: as time after time: as on the other occasions
decisions.reason: He expects things to go as they did each time before (verses 9, 12, 14).

decisions.choice: he said: possibly to himself
decisions.reason: The words may be spoken aloud or only in his mind; Hebrew "said" covers both.

decisions.choice: He said to himself
decisions.reason: Readable takes his words as his thoughts (m3); Literal and Balanced keep "said".

records.source: וַיֹּאחֲז֣וּהוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיְנַקְּר֖וּ אֶת־עֵינָ֑יו וַיּוֹרִ֨ידוּ אוֹת֜וֹ עַזָּ֗תָה וַיַּאַסְר֨וּהוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיְהִ֥י טוֹחֵ֖ן בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֲסוּרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And seized him [the] Philistines and gouged out his eyes and brought him down to Gaza and bound him with the bronze fetters, and he was grinding in [the] house of the prisoners.
pieces: The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes. They took him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze shackles, and he was set to grinding grain in the prison.

L.21: And the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters, and he was grinding in the house of the prisoners.

R.21: The Philistines grabbed Samson and put out his eyes. They took him down to Gaza and put bronze chains on him. They made him grind grain in the prison.

decisions.choice: they gouged out his eyes
decisions.reason: Blinding was done to prisoners of war to make them helpless and to shame them (2 Kings 25:7). Samson's story began with what he saw and wanted (14:1-3); now his eyes are taken.

decisions.choice: grinding in the prison
decisions.reason: Grinding grain with a hand mill was the lowest work, done by slaves and women (Exodus 11:5; Isaiah 47:2). For a warrior it was deep humiliation.

decisions.choice: bronze fetters: a pair of shackles
decisions.reason: The word is "bronze" in a form meaning a pair: two linked bronze bands for the hands or feet.

decisions.choice: grain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what he was grinding, which the Hebrew leaves understood (m2).

records.source: וַיָּ֧חֶל שְׂעַר־רֹאשׁ֛וֹ לְצַמֵּ֖חַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר גֻּלָּֽח׃פ
records.gloss: And began [the] hair of his head to grow as when it had been shaved.
pieces: But the hair of his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.

L.22: And the hair of his head began to grow after it had been shaved.

R.22: But Samson's hair began to grow back after it had been shaved off.

decisions.choice: after it had been shaved: from the time it was shaved
alternatives: just as it had been before it was shaved
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "as soon as" or "after": from the day it was cut, it started growing back.

decisions.choice: his hair began to grow: a hint of what is coming
decisions.reason: The narrator tells the reader something the Philistines ignore. It does not say his strength came back with the hair; in verse 28 Samson asks the LORD for it.

records.source: וְסַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים נֶֽאֱסְפוּ֙לִזְבֹּ֧חַ זֶֽבַח־גָּד֛וֹל לְדָג֥וֹן אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וּלְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ בְּיָדֵ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת שִׁמְשׁ֥וֹן אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] rulers of [the] Philistines gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and for rejoicing, and they said, has given our god into our hand Samson our enemy.
pieces: Now the rulers of the Philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon and to celebrate. \q They said, "Our god has given into our hands \q Samson our enemy."

L.23: And the rulers of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice, \q and they said, "Our god has given into our hand \q Samson our enemy."

R.23: The Philistine rulers came together for a great festival. They offered sacrifices to their god Dagon and celebrated. \q They said, "Our god has handed Samson over to us, \q Samson our enemy!"

decisions.choice: Dagon their god
decisions.reason: Dagon was a chief god of the Philistines, with temples at Gaza and Ashdod (1 Samuel 5:1-7). He was worshiped across the region long before the Philistines came. His name is probably linked to the word for grain, and he was likely a god of crops; the old idea that he was a fish-god rests only on the sound of the Hebrew word for fish and is doubtful.

decisions.choice: Our god has given Samson into our hand
decisions.reason: The Philistines thank Dagon. The reader knows better: Samson fell because the LORD had left him (verse 20), and the LORD will answer his prayer (verses 28-30). The scene becomes a contest between the LORD and Dagon, as again in 1 Samuel 5.

decisions.choice: a chant: a short victory song
decisions.reason: Their words are a chant. In Hebrew the lines end in the same sound, "-enu" ("our"), again and again in verse 24, the kind of verse a crowd would shout together.

decisions.choice: a great festival ... offered sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable says the "great sacrifice" was a religious feast with offerings.

decisions.choice: the chant of verses 23-24 set in lines
decisions.reason: The Philistines' victory chant (m3) is set as poetry. The lines break where the Hebrew accents divide each verse, at the point where the narrator's words give way to the chant, and between the chant's short rhyming phrases.

records.heading: Samson brings down the house of Dagon

records.source: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְהַלְל֖וּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אָמְר֗וּ נָתַ֨ן אֱלֹהֵ֤ינוּ בְיָדֵ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־א֣וֹיְבֵ֔נוּ וְאֵת֙ מַחֲרִ֣יב אַרְצֵ֔נוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְבָּ֖ה אֶת־חֲלָלֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And saw him the people and they praised their god, for they said, has given our god into our hand our enemy and [the] ravager of our land and who multiplied our slain.
pieces: When the people saw him, they praised their god. \q They said, "Our god has given into our hands our enemy, \q the one who laid waste our land \q and killed so many of us."

L.24: And the people saw him, and they praised their god, \q for they said, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy, \q and the one who laid waste our land, \q and who multiplied our slain."

R.24: When the people saw Samson, they praised their god. \q They said, "Our god has handed over to us our enemy, \q the one who ruined our land \q and killed so many of our people!"

decisions.choice: the people saw him
decisions.reason: Samson is brought out only in verse 25, so the story may be telling the crowd's praise ahead of the scene, or the people saw him as he was led in. Either way, the sight of the blind prisoner set them praising Dagon.

decisions.choice: the ravager of our land, who multiplied our slain
decisions.reason: They remember what he did to them: the grain fields, vineyards and olive groves he burned (15:4-5), and the men he killed (14:19; 15:8, 15).

decisions.choice: the chant goes on
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, the lines rhyme in Hebrew on "our": our hand, our enemy, our land, our slain.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּט֣וֹב לִבָּ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ קִרְא֥וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן וִישַֽׂחֶק־לָ֑נוּ וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן מִבֵּ֣ית הָאֲסוּרִ֗ים וַיְצַחֵק֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעֲמִ֥ידוּ אוֹת֖וֹ בֵּ֥ין הָעַמּוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was when [was] good their heart, and they said, call for Samson, and let him make sport for us. And they called for Samson from [the] house of the prisoners, and he made sport before them, and they made stand him between the pillars.
pieces: When they were in high spirits, they said, "Call for Samson, and let him entertain us." So they called Samson out of the prison, and he performed for them. They had him stand between the pillars.

L.25: And it came about, when their hearts were merry, that they said, "Call Samson, that he may entertain us." And they called Samson from the house of the prisoners, and he performed before them; and they made him stand between the pillars.

R.25: The people were having a good time. They said, "Bring Samson out here. Let him do something to make us laugh." So they brought Samson out of the prison, and he entertained them. They made him stand between the pillars of the temple.

decisions.choice: when their hearts were merry: in high spirits
decisions.reason: "A good heart" here means cheerful, often from wine at a feast (1 Samuel 25:36; Esther 1:10).

decisions.choice: let him entertain us
alternatives: let him make sport for us
decisions.reason: The two verbs used here come from the word for laughing. He was made to perform: perhaps feats of strength, perhaps simply to be laughed at as a blind fool. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: when their hearts were merry
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "for [it was] good", and the reading marked in the margin has "when [it was] good". The difference is one letter and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the pillars of the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says that "the house" where this happens is Dagon's temple (verses 26-27).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן אֶל־הַנַּ֨עַר הַמַּחֲזִ֣יק בְּיָדוֹ֮ הַנִּ֣יחָה אוֹתִי֒ וַהֲמִשֵׁ֨נִי֙ אֶת־הָֽעַמֻּדִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הַבַּ֖יִת נָכ֣וֹן עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶשָּׁעֵ֖ן עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Samson to the young man holding his hand, let me rest and let me feel the pillars which the house [is] set on them, and I will lean on them.
pieces: Samson said to the young man who was leading him by the hand, "Let me rest here and feel the pillars that hold up the temple, so that I can lean against them."

L.26: And Samson said to the young man who held him by his hand, "Let me rest, and let me feel the pillars on which the house is set, so that I may lean on them."

R.26: A young servant was holding Samson's hand to lead him. Samson said to him, "Let me feel the pillars that hold up the temple. I want to lean against them and rest."

decisions.choice: the young man: a boy or servant
decisions.reason: The word (na'ar) can mean a boy, a young man, or a servant. Here he is the one guiding the blind prisoner.

decisions.choice: let me rest
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "let me be, leave me" or "let me rest, set me down". Samson asks to stop where he can lean, as a tired prisoner might.

decisions.choice: the pillars on which the house is set
decisions.reason: "The house" is Dagon's temple. Remains of Philistine temples from this time show a roof held up by wooden pillars set on stone bases close together in the middle of the hall. Pull those away, and the roof comes down.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "house", the Hebrew word for a god's house as for any building; Balanced and Readable say "temple".

records.source: וְהַבַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֤א הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וְהַנָּשִׁ֔ים וְשָׁ֕מָּה כֹּ֖ל סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְעַל־הַגָּ֗ג כִּשְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֔ה הָרֹאִ֖ים בִּשְׂח֥וֹק שִׁמְשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: And the house [was] full [of] the men and the women, and there [were] all [the] rulers of [the] Philistines, and on the roof about three thousand man and woman, the [ones] looking at [the] performing of Samson.
pieces: The temple was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the Philistines were there. On the roof there were about 3,000 men and women looking on as Samson performed.

L.27: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the Philistines [were] there, and on the roof [were] about 3,000 men and women, watching while Samson performed.

R.27: The temple was crowded with men and women. All the Philistine rulers were there. About 3,000 more men and women were up on the roof. They were all watching Samson entertain them.

decisions.choice: about 3,000 on the roof
decisions.reason: Roofs were flat and could hold a crowd. The people on the roof watched Samson below, which tells how great the fall of the building would be.

decisions.choice: all the rulers of the Philistines
decisions.reason: All five rulers who had bought Samson's betrayal are present, which sets up the end in verse 30.

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: As in verse 26.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֥א שִׁמְשׁ֛וֹן אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יֱהֹוִ֡ה זָכְרֵ֣נִי נָא֩ וְחַזְּקֵ֨נִי נָ֜א אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֤עַם הַזֶּה֙ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאִנָּקְמָ֧ה נְקַם־אַחַ֛ת מִשְּׁתֵ֥י עֵינַ֖י מִפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And called Samson to YHWH and said, my Lord YHWH, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this time, the God, and I will avenge myself [with] vengeance of one for my two eyes from [the] Philistines.
pieces: Then Samson called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, please remember me. Please give me strength just this once more, O God, so that with one blow I may pay the Philistines back for my two eyes."

L.28: And Samson called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, O God, so that I may avenge myself on the Philistines with one vengeance for my two eyes."

R.28: Then Samson prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, please remember me. God, please make me strong just one more time. Then I can pay back the Philistines for my two eyes, all at one time."

decisions.choice: the LORD; Lord GOD; God
decisions.reason: Samson calls on the LORD by his name (YHWH), as "my Lord YHWH" (Adonai YHWH), and as God (ha-elohim). Where the name follows "Lord" it is read aloud as "God", so the two words are not both read as "Lord".

decisions.choice: remember me
decisions.reason: In prayer, "remember" means more than recall: it asks God to act for someone (Genesis 8:1; 30:22; 1 Samuel 1:19). It is Samson's first prayer since his thirst at Lehi (15:18).

decisions.choice: one act of vengeance for my two eyes
alternatives: vengeance for one of my two eyes
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "one vengeance for my two eyes", a single blow to repay both, or as "vengeance for one of my two eyes", as if all he could do would not repay both. The first is followed here.

decisions.choice: Samson prays for revenge
decisions.reason: He asks to pay back what was done to him. The narrator neither praises nor blames the request; the LORD answers it, and through it Samson does what he was born for, to begin to save Israel from the Philistines (13:5).

decisions.choice: prayed to
decisions.reason: Calling to the LORD here is prayer, so Readable says "prayed".

records.source: וַיִּלְפֹּ֨ת שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י׀עַמּוּדֵ֣י הַתָּ֗וֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַבַּ֨יִת֙ נָכ֣וֹן עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּסָּמֵ֖ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד בִּימִינ֖וֹ וְאֶחָ֥ד בִּשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And grasped Samson [the] two pillars of the middle which the house [was] set on them, and he leaned on them, one in his right and one in his left.
pieces: Samson took hold of the two middle pillars on which the temple stood, and he braced himself against them, his right hand on one and his left hand on the other.

L.29: And Samson grasped the two middle pillars on which the house was set, and he braced himself against them, one with his right [hand] and one with his left.

R.29: Samson reached out and found the two pillars in the middle of the temple. They held up the whole building. He set his right hand against one pillar and his left against the other, and he leaned on them with all his weight.

decisions.choice: grasped: took firm hold
decisions.reason: The verb means to clasp or to twist; in Ruth 3:8 it is used of turning over. Here Samson wraps his hands around the pillars.

decisions.choice: one with his right and one with his left
decisions.reason: "Hand" is understood: one pillar under each hand.

decisions.choice: [hand] (L); hand (B, R); They held up the whole building (R)
decisions.reason: The word the Hebrew leaves understood is supplied (m2). Readable also says why these pillars mattered (verse 26).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן תָּמ֣וֹת נַפְשִׁי֮ עִם־פְּלִשְׁתִּים֒ וַיֵּ֣ט בְּכֹ֔חַ וַיִּפֹּ֤ל הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַל־הַסְּרָנִ֔ים וְעַל־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־בּ֑וֹ וַיִּהְי֤וּ הַמֵּתִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵמִ֣ית בְּמוֹת֔וֹ רַבִּ֕ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵמִ֖ית בְּחַיָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Samson, let die my soul with [the] Philistines. And he stretched out with strength, and fell the house on the rulers and on all the people that [was] in it. And were the dead whom he killed in his death many more than whom he had killed in his life.
pieces: And Samson said, "Let me die together with the Philistines!" He pushed with all his might, and down came the temple on the rulers and on all the people inside. So he killed more people by his death than he had killed during his whole life.

L.30: And Samson said, "Let my soul die with the Philistines!" And he stretched out with [all his] strength, and the house fell on the rulers and on all the people who [were] in it. And the dead whom he killed at his death were more than those whom he had killed in his life.

R.30: Samson said, "Let me die together with the Philistines!" Then he pushed as hard as he could. The temple fell down on the rulers and on everyone in it. Samson killed more people when he died than he had killed while he was alive.

decisions.choice: let my soul die: let me die
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) here is the person's life or self; "let my soul die" means simply "let me die".

decisions.choice: Samson's death with the Philistines
decisions.reason: Samson does not die in despair; he dies doing what he was born for, striking the Philistines (13:5). He is later named among those who acted by faith (Hebrews 11:32).

decisions.choice: he stretched out with strength: he pushed hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to stretch out or bend. He threw all his strength against the two pillars.

decisions.choice: he killed more people by his death than during his life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Samson the subject of the closing sentence, which says the same thing more simply than "the dead whom he killed ... were more".

records.source: וַיֵּרְד֨וּ אֶחָ֜יו וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִיהוּ֮ וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ אֹתוֹ֒ וַֽיַּעֲל֣וּ׀וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אוֹת֗וֹ בֵּ֤ין צָרְעָה֙ וּבֵ֣ין אֶשְׁתָּאֹ֔ל בְּקֶ֖בֶר מָנ֣וֹחַ אָבִ֑יו וְה֛וּא שָׁפַ֥ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And went down his brothers and all [the] house of his father and lifted him, and they brought up and buried him between Zorah and between Eshtaol in [the] tomb of Manoah his father. And he had judged Israel twenty year[s].
pieces: Then his brothers and all his father's family came down. They took him and brought him back up, and they buried him in the tomb of Manoah his father, between Zorah and Eshtaol. He had judged Israel for twenty years.

L.31: And his brothers and all the house of his father came down and took him, and they brought [him] up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he had judged Israel twenty years.

R.31: Then Samson's brothers and his father's whole family came down to Gaza. They took his body and carried it back home. They buried him in his father Manoah's tomb, between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson had led Israel for twenty years.

decisions.choice: buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in Manoah's tomb
decisions.reason: His story ends where it began: the Spirit of the LORD first stirred him "between Zorah and Eshtaol" (13:25). Burial in the family tomb mattered greatly; the man who lived among foreigners is laid with his father.

decisions.choice: his brothers
decisions.reason: Samson was his mother's first child (13:2-3). "Brothers" may be younger brothers born later, or close relatives, as the word often means.

decisions.choice: he had judged Israel twenty years
decisions.reason: As at 2:16, a judge was a leader raised up to rescue and govern Israel. The same total closes the account of his deeds in 15:20, "in the days of the Philistines"; here it ends his life. The Philistines still ruled Israel when he died (13:1, 5).

decisions.choice: to Gaza; his body; back home; led Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says where they went and what they carried, and uses "led" for "judged" as at 2:16. Balanced supplies "him" for the object Literal brackets.
